name: Level_2 - Task_3
description:
Investigate whether a MACE model can learn a silver-dimer reference dataset and support a short bulk-silver simulation. Use the supplied MACE-MP-0 checkpoint named by teacher_model in /workspace/models, with dispersion enabled, to label 45 isolated, nonperiodic Ag2 structures with separations from 0.6 to 5.0 Å in 0.1 Å increments. Save the structures, total energies in eV, and complete atomic forces in eV/Å.

Starting from the supplied MACE-MP-0b checkpoint named by student_model in /workspace/models, fine-tune on all 45 labeled structures. Choose and document training settings, numerical precision, and a validation strategy appropriate to this dataset. Quantify energy agreement per atom and force agreement with the teacher before and after training, including aggregate errors and their dependence on separation. Clearly distinguish fitting diagnostics on training data from evidence of generalization. Save a loadable trained checkpoint and training history sufficient to establish that optimization occurred and to reproduce the reported diagnostics.

Build periodic FCC silver using a conventional four-atom cubic cell with lattice parameter 4.09 Å repeated 3 × 3 × 3, giving 108 atoms. Keep the cell fixed and use the fine-tuned model for a 5 ps simulation targeting 300 K. Initialize velocities at 300 K with a recorded random seed, remove center-of-mass momentum once, and do not reinitialize velocities during the run. Choose and justify the thermostat, integration timestep, and sampling. Quantify temperature behavior and assess physical stability using energies, forces, and structural evolution. Discuss the limitations of transferring a dimer-trained model to bulk silver; report instability or poor agreement honestly rather than assuming successful transfer.

Submit a manifest linking the labeled dataset, trained checkpoint, training and MD logs, scripts, settings, and structured JSON analysis data. Include trajectory data containing cell, positions, momenta, time, potential energies, and forces, sampled sufficiently to reproduce the temperature and stability assessment. Record input checkpoint identities and the provenance of the trained model.
submission_format:
Fill in the blank manifest below and submit its path inside the task workspace
(for example, output/manifest.json). Linked paths may be relative to the manifest.
Replace null, empty strings and arrays with your results, file paths and data;
repeat example records and replace <...> keys with your actual identifiers.
Fixed units and method names describe the illustrated format. Where the task
leaves a method open, choose and record your method. Retain raw evidence and
calculations for any alternative method; unsupported calculations require
independent review before a final score.
